title: One dispatcher comparison step
statement: Let the dispatcher for $n$ procedures occur at position $\mathrm{disp}$ in a word-RAM program of word size $W$. If $j<n$, the one-register contains the word encoding $1$, and $v-1$ lies in the signed range $-2^{W-1}\le v-1<2^{W-1}$, then from program counter $\mathrm{disp}+2j$ with the return-register containing the word encoding $v$, two machine steps reach a configuration whose return-register contains the word encoding $v-1$. Its program counter is $j$ if $v-1<0$, and otherwise is $\mathrm{disp}+2(j+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: Code at disp begins with the dispatcher for n procedures
